Associated Note: Performance Intervention Summary The coaching session was conducted to address client feedback received from Crystal regarding attendance concerns, End-of-Day (EOD) reporting compliance, responsiveness, and communication practices. The discussion primarily focused on an incident dated April 24, where a gap in activity was identified after Mitch reportedly went on break at 3:23 PM and returned at 5:32 PM, creating a concern around a possible overbreak and online presence issue. Crystal also raised concerns regarding inconsistent EOD submissions, delayed reporting, and repeated follow-ups needed to close tasks or receive updates, which were escalated as concerns around insubordination and accountability. During the discussion, Mitch explained that the April 24 incident was unintentional and likely related to forgetting to resume Time Doctor tracking after lunch. Mitch shared that Time Doctor automatically turns off after periods of inactivity and clarified that there was no deliberate intention to extend the break or stop working. However, Mitch acknowledged that no proactive communication or notification was sent at the time to explain the time gap, which Mayee identified as a key communication lapse that likely contributed to the escalation. A significant portion of the discussion focused on EOD compliance and reporting expectations. Mitch explained that detailed EODs are regularly submitted through Superhuman, using a personally developed reporting structure that includes work orders, pending tasks, and property updates. Mitch expressed frustration that some information being repeatedly requested by leadership had already been documented in prior updates and noted that clients often review EODs the following day. Despite this, Mayee clarified that an EOD is intended to function as an official end-of-shift sign-off, and therefore should be submitted daily and immediately after shift completion, rather than the following morning. The coaching emphasized that relying solely on written updates without proactive communication may create perception gaps between work completed and client visibility. The conversation also explored operational and workload-related challenges impacting performance. Mitch shared concerns about being the sole person managing maintenance-related responsibilities, resulting in a high volume of work orders, move-ins, move-outs, property concerns, and follow-ups. Mitch noted that delays in external processes and previous staffing transitions have added pressure to the role, while also expressing concern over the recent termination of other VAs despite receiving positive feedback beforehand. Mayee acknowledged the workload concerns and recognized that bandwidth and workload distribution may be contributing factors to responsiveness and communication gaps. To support improvement and alignment, several next steps were discussed. Mitch committed to sending EOD reports consistently at the end of every shift, proactively communicating attendance or task-related delays, and copying coaching support on reporting for monitoring purposes. Mayee committed to documenting the coaching discussion, reviewing Mitch’s April EOD submissions for trend analysis, and providing Crystal with context and feedback gathered during the session. Additional recommendations included requesting weekly feedback sessions with Crystal to better align expectations and performance standards, as well as revisiting workload allocation given Mitch’s independent handling of the role. The session concluded with a reminder that the concerns raised by Crystal are currently being treated seriously due to references to final written warning and insubordination, and that future occurrences of similar issues may result in corrective action at the HR level. However, the coaching remained focused on providing support, ensuring fairness, and helping Mitch improve communication, compliance, and overall client alignment moving forward.

Better Task Organization Riva began proactively reviewing overdue tasks, preparing earlier for month-end deliverables, and applying more structured prioritization. Improved Accuracy & Attention to Detail There was stronger awareness around verification steps, particularly in vendor setup, invoice handling, and hard cost tracking. Stronger Accountability Riva consistently remained responsive, engaged in feedback discussions, and actively implemented recommendations from prior sessions.
